title: Embryonic development and volumetric growth of the Florida stone crab, Menippe mercenaria Say 1818 (Decapoda: Brachyura: Menippidae)
content:
Abstract
Embryonic development is an important but often under-documented component of crustacean life history. Florida stone crabs (Menippe mercenaria Say 1818) support one of the most valuable crustacean fisheries in the southeastern United States; however, fine-scale descriptions of embryogenesis for the species remain limited. We established a quantitative baseline of stone crab embryonic development by monitoring embryos from extrusion to hatch across two reproductive seasons. Changes in egg size, volume, coloration, and morphology, allowed development to be partitioned into a series of distinct morphological stages. Egg mass coloration shifted predictably throughout development, providing a visible indicator of underlying morphological progression. Embryonic growth and developmental rate differed between seasons, with embryos from the elevated-temperature cohort developing approximately two days faster. These differences are consistent with the thermal plasticity reported in other brachyuran species but may also reflect seasonal variation in broodstock collected earlier in the reproductive season, which covaried with temperature. This study provides the first comprehensive morphological characterization of Florida stone crab embryogenesis, establishing a developmental framework for comparative analyses, fisheries management and reproductive assessment.
